     RELATED CODE SECTIONS & RESOURCES: BC 3307.6.4.4, Item 7

    I. BACKGROUND
       Section 3307.6.4.4, Item 7 of the 2022 New York City Building Code requires “a horizontal span of at
       least 10 feet (3048 mm), as measured down the length of the sidewalk, walkway, or pathway” to be
       provided between vertical members of certain sidewalk sheds. This bulletin provides guidance
       concerning this measurement.


    II. MEASUREMENT
       The measurement shall be taken from the centerline of the vertical member.
       Where a pipe or column is utilized as a vertical member, the centerline shall be through the center of
       the pipe or column. (See Figure 1)

                                            Figure 1: Sidewalk shed pipes (in plan view)




         NOTE: 10’ distance is minimum, except where a shorter distance is required to avoid obstructions. See Section III for more information.

     Where a mast section, lattice tower, or similar element is utilized as a vertical member, the centerline
     shall be through the center of the entire structure. (See Figure 2)

                                         Figure 2: Sidewalk shed towers (in plan view)




       NOTE: 10’ distance is minimum, except where a shorter distance is required to avoid obstructions. See Section III for more information.

                   * Mast sections, lattice towers, or similar elements that exceed 24” x 24” require approval of the Commissioner.


   III. SHORTER DISTANCE
     BC 3307.6.4.4, Item 7 requires the horizontal span to be at least 10 feet. However, the span may be
     shorter if needed to avoid the curb or obstructions such as curb cuts or ramps, vehicular access points,
     streetlights, traffic lights or signs, fire hydrants, fire department connections, water sampling stations,
     bus shelters, street furniture, trees, adjacent show windows, means of ingress/egress, subway
     entrances, or access points to vaults, manholes, or other underground structures. Sidewalk shed plans
     shall include locations of such obstructions and indicate measurement of shorter spans.
